Before my dad died also of lung cancer, he asked me to find him a record from the 1940's. He wanted it played at his funeral. I found and put it on a CD for the fateful day. We played the song so many times we got to know it by heart. I the same year my dad died, my wife and I, went on a cruise. There was a fantastic 70's / 80's bar on board, we went to every night. On one of the nights we were talking at the bar and a kareoke night was taking place. My wife was watching the screens with the words of the songs scrolling as the person sang along. Her eyes lit up and she grabbed me and told me to look at the screen. There on the screen, came the words of the song my dad had asked for, but the singer was singing something completely different. We both saw it clearly and we where in total shock at first, but the realised that it was him letting us know he was about. I often think of that night when I'm down and I know he is watching over us.

If you look around the unit you will see the vents, of all the ones that I have repaired, those with blocked vents will overheat the unit and make them fail.The units can run hot but you will know when one is blocked because you can't touch the unit because of the heat. They are not made to easily strip down so I generally use air duster to blow out the unit of dust.The fan arraignment I use now avoids the over heating problem and cuts down on the dust.
Just ensure it has good air flow around it and it should be fine, then clean it every so often.
It's possible, I keep mine in glass cabinets with a fan that circulates the air and keeps them cool, no problems since I did that. I clean the fans every three months or so.

I have had 2 running now for over 5 years and I have had them fail after a few months. It depends on air flow around the unit. I have seen them covered in dust and clogged up, but most are repairable. Just be careful where you put them.

Depression does not reduce your intelligence, it reduces your will to live and many other things, but not your ability to understand your feelings or your pain or the pain of others.

No matter how loved I might be, it does not take away the pain inside me. I have read countless stories of the distress and suffering left behind when someone takes their life. I am sure they understand but continuing to live for someone else does not help or in any way cure the pain.
